title: Raspberry Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: All-cream custard with sieved raspberry purée stirred in; no milk or vanilla.
summary: Based on our classic custard but made with cream alone, then mixed with a sweet-sharp raspberry purée that is sieved to remove the seeds. Vivid pink and full of fruit.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
lemon juice, plus more to taste
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the custard
steps.text: Simmer the cream with the 130 g sugar and salt until the sugar dissolves. Whisk the yolks, temper with a third of the cream and return to the pan.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Stir over low heat until the custard reaches 77-80 °C and coats the spatula. Strain into a bowl.

steps.title: Blend the berries
steps.text: Blend the raspberries with the 40 g sugar, lemon juice and pinch of salt. It should be sweet with a tart edge; adjust with more sugar or juice.

steps.title: Sieve in
steps.text: Press the purée through the sieve into the custard to catch the seeds, then stir well.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cool in the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn, then freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Frozen raspberries work very well; thaw them fully first.
A common mistake is skipping the sieve, leaving the ice cream full of hard seeds.
The same method works with strawberries; there is no need to sieve them.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks.
